FORE WORD This Indian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Ferro Alloys SectionaI Committee had been approved by the Metallurgical Engineering Division Council. The Committee felt to formulate a standard on the chemical analysis of ferrosilicon-magnesium alloy in two parts that is, Part 1 covering determination of silicon by gravimetric method and Part 2 covering determination of calcium and magnesium by EDTA method. While finalizing Part 1 of IS 14529 `Chemical analysis of ferrosilicon-magnesium alloy: Part 1 Determination of silicon by gravimetric method', the Committee decided to have a single standard by merging Part 1 into Part 2 of 1S 14529 `Chemical analysis of ferrosilicon-magnesium alloy: Part 2 Determination of calcium and magnesium', which was first published in 1998. This standard supersedes 1S 14529 (Part 2) :1998,

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)'. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

Y SCOPE This standard describes the method for determination of calcium in the range 0.25 to 3.0 percent, magnesium in the range from 2 to 25 percent by EDTA method and silicon in the range 45 to 75 percent by gravimetric method in ferrosilicon magnesium alloy. 2 REFERENCES The standards listed below contain provisions, which through reference in this text, constitute provisions of this standard. Calcium is titrated with disodium (ethylene dinitrilo) tetra acetate (EDTA) at pH 12. Magnesium plus calcium is titrated with EDTA at pH 10.0 and magnesium concentration is calculated by correcting for the volume of EDTA required to titrate the calcium. 5.2 Reagents 5.2.1 Ammonium Chloride BuferSolution (pH 10.0) -- Dissolve 60 g of amonium chloride in 200 ml water, add 570 ml of ammonium hydroxide and dilute to 1 Iitre. 5.2.2 Standard Calcium Solution (1 ml= 0.2002 mg Ca) -- Dissolve 0.500 g of dried calcium carbonate (purity 99.9 percent, &fin) in 100 ml of dilute hydrochloric acid (5 percent). 5.2.5 Hydroxy Napthol Blue Mixture -- Mix 1.0 g of indicator with 100 g sodium chloride and mix thoroughly. 5.2.6 Magnesium Chloride Solution (2.5 g/m[) -- Dissolve 0.25 g of magnesium chloride hexahydrate in 50 ml water and dilute to 100 ml. 5.2.7 Potassium Cyanide Solution (50 g/1) -- Dissolve 2 g of potassium hydroxide in water and add 5 g of potassium cyanide to it, dilute to 100 ml and transfer to a plastic bottle.
NOTE -- Caution -- The preparation, storage and use of potassium cyanide require care and attention. Avoid inhalation of fomes aod exposure of the skin to the chemical and its solutions. Works in a well ventilated hood.

5.2.8 Potassium Hydroxide Bufler Solution (pH 12.5) -- Dissolve 531 g of potassium hydroxide in water, add 50 g of potassium cyanide and dilute to 1 Iitre. Store the solution in a plastic bottle. 5.2.9 Triethanolomine Solution (200 mill) -- Dilute 20 ml of triethanolamine to 100 ml of water. 5.3 Procedure 5.3.1 Weigh accurately 1.0 g of sample and transfer to a dry TFE -- fluorocarbon beaker. Add 10 ml of nitric acid. Cautiously add 10 ml of hydrofluoric acid and heat gently till the sample is dissolved. Wash the sides of the beaker with a fine stream of water. Add 20 ml of perch loric acid, place on a hot plate at a temperature not exceeding 3000C and evaporate to dense fumes of perch loric acid. Cool, add 10 ml of dilute hydrochloric acid (1: 1) and heat to dissolve the salts. Transfer to a 600 ml beaker and evaporate to moderate dryness on a hot plate. Place on a burner and evaporate to complete dryness. Add 20 ml of dilute hydrochloric acid (1: 1), wash the sides of the beaker with a tine stream of water and heat to dissolve the salts. 5.3.2 Add 200 ml of water and 5 g of ammonium chloride. Boil and cool. Add ammonium hydroxide until the iron begins to precipitate and continue addition dropwise till the precipitation is completed. Cool to room temperature, transfer to a 500 ml volumetric flask, dilute to volume, and mix. Let it stand for 1 h to allow the precipitate to settle. 2

5.3.6 Add 5 ml of triethanolamine solution stir and immediately add 10 ml of ammonium chloride buffer solution. Add 5 ml of potassium cyanide solution (see Note) and 3 to 5 drops of erichrome black T solution. Titrate with EDTA solution (0.005 M) to the disappearance of last trace of the red colour.
NOTE -- In going through the end point, the colour changes from red to blue to blue green.

to the crucible to stir up any unattached particles of alloy on the bottom or sides. The crucible and contents being maintained at a low red heat. Just before completion of fusion, the temperature is increased to bright redness for a minute.

Sample is decomposed by fusion with sodium peroxide and sodium carbonate and silica is separated by dehydration, from the acidified extract. Any silica remaining in the filtrate is precipitated alongwith ferric hydroxide by precipitation with ammonium hydroxide and then dehydrated by fuming with perchloric acid. After ignition, the combined silica residues are treated with hydrofluoric acid and silicon determined by volatilization as silicon tetrafluoride. 6.2 Reagents 6.2.1 Sodium Peroxide, solid. 6.2.2 Sodium Carbonate, 6.2.3 Dilute Hydrochloric 6.2.4 Concentrated (see 1S 265). 6.2.5 Ammonium anhydrous. Acid, 2:98, 1:10,5:95 (v/v).

6.3.2 When the crucible has cooled for the molten mass to solidifi, slowly drop the crucible with its solidified melt in 50 ml of cold water in a 500 ml PTFE beaker and cover the beaker immediately by PTFE cover glass. When the reaction has subsided, take out the crucible and the lid and wash them thoroughly, first with warm dilute hydrochloric acid (10 percent,v/v) and then with water, collecting the washings in the same PTFE beaker. Acidify the extract by concentrated hydrochloric acid and transfer the solution to a 500 ml beaker. 6.3.3 Insert glass rod into the solution, add 40 ml (or even more if necessary) sulphuric acid (1:1) and evaporate to fumes. Allow to cool and add 200 ml of dilute hydrochloric acid (1 :9). Heat until salts are in solution and filter through a paper pulp pad. Wash with dilute hydrochloric acid (5:95) and finally with hot water till it is free from chlorides. Transfer the residue to a platinum crucible and preserve. 6.3,4 Add to the filtrate and washings reserved in 6.3.3, 5 g of ammonium chloride, heat nearly to boiling and precipitate with ammonia solution (1: 1). Heat to boiling, filter through a medium textured filter paper and wash with hot water. Transfer the precipitate and paper to the original beaker, add 30 ml of concentrated nitric acid and 10 ml of dilute sulphuric acid (1:1) and evaporate to fumes. Cool and add 20 ml of concentrated hydrochloric acid, 100 ml of water and heat until the salts are in solution. Filter through medium textured filter paper, wash as before and transfer the pad to the platinum crucible containing the first silica residue. Ignite at low temperature and finally at 1 100"C to 1 150"C to constant mass (A) in a muffle furnace. 6.3.5 Moisten the residue with 1 ml of dilute sr.dphuric acid (1:4) and add 10 ml of hydrofluoric acid, evaporate to dryness, ignite at 1 100�C to 1 150�C, cool and weigh (B). 6.3.6 same same result Carry out a blank determination following the procedure as specified in 6.3.1 to 6.3.5 and using amount of all the reagents and correct the final for the blank value, if any.
